    Propagating BGRS critical-path radical sandwiches #

    Fix one occurrence-by-occurrence representative of a singular path whose ordinary composite is zero. At a cut, property P_i is then exactly the assertion that inserting some middle Jacobson-radical endomorphism gives a nonzero composite: membership of the zero full composite in the sandwich is automatic.

    This file proves the rightward one-arrow induction step from BGRS 4.2. The zero composite and nonzero sandwich prohibit cotransit/transit for the two cut pieces. Roiter's one-dimensional middle-sandwich conclusion and stability of the enlarged prefix force cotransit across the next arrow, after which the radical coefficient transfers to the next cut.

        Conditional on Roiter's transit lemma, every split of the middle of a critical spine carries the exact P_i zero-representative cut. This is the all-internal-cuts conclusion of BGRS 4.2; the sole unproved source input is the HasRoiterTransitRankBound instance.

        Conditional on Roiter's rank-one transit consequence, every arrow strictly inside a critical path allows both transit and cotransit. This is the bitransit conclusion in BGRS 4.2, stated for the quotient-chosen ordinary representative of the displayed ray arrow.
